# mm-mcp

> mm-mcp is an MCP server for Mattermost. It lets an AI agent read and search a person's Mattermost and, once they allow it, post and reply, as them or as a bot. It runs on the person's own machine, started by their MCP client over stdio, and talks to nothing but their Mattermost server.

This file is for an AI agent asked to set mm-mcp up for a person. The pages below have the details.

## Setting it up for a person

1. Install mm-mcp with the package manager the machine has: `brew install vriesdemichael/tap/mm-mcp` (macOS, Linux), `winget install vriesdemichael.mm-mcp` or `scoop bucket add vriesdemichael https://github.com/vriesdemichael/scoop` then `scoop install vriesdemichael/mm-mcp` (Windows). A shell started before the install may not find `mm-mcp`; start a new one, and check with `mm-mcp version`.
2. Get the address the person opens Mattermost at, such as `https://chat.example.com`.
3. Keep a credential in the system's credential store, never in a file or the conversation:
   - The person has a personal access token or a bot token: they run `mm-mcp login --with paste --url <address>` in a terminal they type in, and paste it at the prompt. Never ask for the token, and never pass it as an argument or an environment variable yourself.
   - Otherwise: run `mm-mcp login --url <address>`. It may open the person's browser to approve mm-mcp, or a browser window at their sign-in page, where they log in themselves. It waits up to ten minutes: give it that long, or run it in the background, and tell the person first what will open. A password or token prompt cannot be answered from your shell; mm-mcp then says to run it in a terminal the person types in.
   - On success it prints `Logged in to <address> as @<username>` and exits 0. When nothing works it exits 1, after a summary of each way it tried and what to do next: read that to the person.
4. Check: `mm-mcp doctor --url <address> --json` exits 1 when a check failed, and says what to fix.
5. Add the server to the person's MCP client, with only `MM_URL` in its environment (below). Do not set `MM_TOKEN` when a login is stored.
6. Restart the client, or reconnect the server, then call the `get_me` tool. It answers with the person's Mattermost user.

Writes are off until the person allows them with `MM_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=true`. Turn that on only when they ask. Each post others will see then asks the person first, through a form the client shows; in a client that does not show it, such as the Claude desktop app, `MM_MCP_ASK_BEFORE_WRITES=false` leaves the asking to the client's own approval.

## Adding the server to a client

mm-mcp is a local MCP server over stdio:

- command: `mm-mcp`
- arguments: `serve`
- environment: `MM_URL` set to the address; nothing else is needed once a login is stored

Add it the way the person's MCP client adds a stdio server, as that client's own documentation says, under a name such as `mattermost`. Two Mattermost servers are two such servers, under two names, each with its own `MM_URL`.

mm-mcp also ships, for the person to install themselves:

- a Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add vriesdemichael/mm-mcp`, then `/plugin install mm-mcp@mm-mcp`. Use it or add the server yourself, not both.
- a Claude Desktop bundle: the `.mcpb` file for their machine from https://github.com/vriesdemichael/mm-mcp/releases/latest, opened in Claude Desktop, with the token left empty. mm-mcp must still be installed with a package manager for `mm-mcp login`.

The other settings, such as allowing writes, are environment variables too: https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/configuration/

## Docs

- [Installation](https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/installation/): installing, a credential, each client, first steps
- [Logging in](https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/login/): `mm-mcp login`, every way it logs in, and what each failure means
- [Configuration](https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/configuration/): every environment variable and command
- [Tools](https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/tools/): every tool, and what it asks before it writes
- [Security](https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/security/): what leaves the machine, credentials, and what an agent can do
- [For administrators](https://vriesdemichael.github.io/mm-mcp/administrators/): letting mm-mcp in, and recognising it
